summary.title: Build Your Own Redis: Ping <-> Pong [2/4]
summary.one_liner: You learn the basics of the Redis Protocol (RESP) and how to make a toy Ruby TCP server answer a PING command with PONG, verified by an integration test using redis-rb.
keywords: how does redis client server communication work
takeaways: RESP encodes data by a leading type byte: + for simple strings, $ for bulk strings, * for arrays.
Bulk strings are binary-safe because the byte length is sent upfront, so embedded \r\n is allowed.
Redis commands are sent from clients as arrays of bulk strings, e.g. PING is *1 with $4 PING.
A minimal server can pass a PING integration test by always writing +PONG\r\n, but it cheats by ignoring the actual command.
summary.summary: This second article in a four-part series builds a toy Redis clone in Ruby. It explains the Redis Protocol (RESP) with examples of simple strings, bulk strings, and arrays, and shows how redis-cli commands are encoded on the wire. It then writes an integration test using redis-rb against the official Redis and the custom server on port 6380, and makes the test pass by having the server always reply +PONG. The author notes this cheats, since ECHO also gets PONG, and defers proper command handling to later articles.
